detail: Between 5% and 10% below the high counts as a pullback, and the S&P 500 closed at 7,175.83 on Thursday, about 8.2% below its record close of 7,818.93 on 6 October. It has now fallen six days running, its longest losing streak since 2024; dips of this size happen in most years.
source: Reuters closing figures, 19 Nov; record close from Anadolu and EdgeX, 6 Oct

detail: Breadth was narrow on Thursday: on the Nasdaq 3,756 shares fell and only 1,057 rose, about 3.6 fallers for every riser. When most shares fall together, the selling is wide rather than limited to a few big names.
Above 4.5% counts as high, and the US 10-year yield eased slightly to about 5.05% on Thursday after softer US factory and jobs figures. Safe bonds paying over 5% set a high bar for shares to beat.
source: US Treasury data via market recaps, 19 Nov

detail: Markets expect rates to go up: CME FedWatch put the chance of a quarter-point Fed rise on 9 December at about 96% on Thursday, and traders see about an 80% chance of a Bank of England rise on 17 December. Higher rates make borrowing dearer and tend to weigh on share prices, especially fast-growing companies.
source: CME FedWatch via Reuters, 19 Nov; LSEG data via Reuters, 18 Nov

detail: Above $90 a barrel counts as expensive, and Brent crude settled almost unchanged at $91.98 on Thursday as reports of tankers hit by mines in the Strait of Hormuz offset signs of plentiful supply. Dear oil keeps pressure on inflation, which is one reason central banks are raising rates.
